description:
Description: Our weather or climate system is a high-dimensional, multi-scale, chaotic, dynamical system which presents a challenging problem for fully data-driven models to perform forecasting. Any forecasting pipeline requires the data-driven model to integrate information from the observations of the system to have an initial condition from where it starts forecasting. However, observations from the system are usually noisy and sparse and the purpose of a data assimilation algorithm is to ensure that information from both the background forecast (coming from the forecasting model) and the noisy observations are properly weighed to estimate an accurate state of the system to be used as an initial condition. In this work, we explore a few efforts in building data-driven models for weather forecasting and developing hybrid (data-driven + numerical) data assimilation algorithms for enhanced computation of initial states and improved accuracy in forecasting.

Bio: Ashesh Chattopadhyay (https://sites.google.com/view/ashesh6810/home) did his bachelor’s from the department of Mechanical Engineering at Indian Institute of Technology, Patna where he worked primarily in optimization and computational geometry for fluid interface modeling. He got his masters from the University of Texas, El Paso, from the Computational Science program where his research was focused on high performance computing. Since then, he has been a PhD student at Rice University in the department of Mechanical Engineering, where he works at the intersection of theoretical deep learning, dynamical systems, and turbulence modeling for broad applications in forecasting atmospheric dynamics and extreme weather. During his PhD, he has spent a year and a half at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory as a research intern/affiliate working in different areas of geometric and generative deep learning for stochastic emulation of Earth system models.
